title: El Salvador Tax Incentives: Who Qualifies for Up to 10 Years of Relief?

lines: A tax incentive can improve your return.
But can it turn a weak location into a good investment?
Here's who qualifies, who actually benefits, and what's left after location and execution costs.
In El Salvador, qualifying new investments in San Salvador's defined Historic Center may receive up to ten years of income-tax relief.
That's a specific regime for a specific area, not a nationwide rule.
And not every business qualifies.
Start with three checks.
Location: inside the defined perimeter. One block outside can change the answer.
Investment: an eligible activity, such as food, lodging, or restoration, above the minimum.
Approval: the Planning Authority must qualify the project. No approval, no benefit.
Then ask who receives it.
Owner, operator, and developer are often different companies.
A landlord's qualification doesn't automatically cut a tenant's taxes.
Here's a simplified, hypothetical annual comparison, after tax.
Thirty thousand dollars of assumed tax savings, minus twenty-four thousand in added after-tax occupancy costs, leaves six thousand a year.
It leaves out other costs, timing, and risk. It's not a Salvadoran tax calculation or a promised return.
Demand, permits, utilities, and opening delays can erase a thin advantage.
Underwrite the base case without incentives, and show the benefit separately.
